chapters.title: A renewal recommendation is not a rate approval
chapters.takeaway: Maturity timing, payment shock, competitor gap, relationship depth, branch capacity, privacy, and approval authority shape what a bank can recommend for review.

chapters.title: Connect every kind of intelligence to the renewal choice
chapters.takeaway: People, governed renewal facts, operating guidance, and current public context come together through one governed intelligence platform.

chapters.title: The renewal team has one review brief to prepare
chapters.takeaway: A mortgage renewal strategy lead for {{ organization_name }} must turn maturity workload, risk signals, branch capacity, and offer guardrails into a defensible review brief.

chapters.title: Start with what the renewal teams already know
chapters.takeaway: Meeting notes, executive questions, accountable owners, and unresolved branch or pricing escalations establish the practical decision context before the numbers are read.
chapters.prompt: Catch me up before the renewal review. What commitments, executive questions, branch constraints, and approval follow-ups are open for this week?

chapters.title: Trace renewal pressure to governed measures
chapters.takeaway: Fabric IQ connects maturity workload, balances, branch capacity, payment shock, derived attrition risk, renewal likelihood, and offer coverage without exposing customer-level details by default.
chapters.prompt: Using the governed renewal model, where are maturity workload, payment shock, value at risk, and offer coverage creating the most pressure?

chapters.title: Apply pricing and approval rules before recommending action
chapters.takeaway: Offer catalogue, pricing, escalation, suitability, privacy, and workflow guidance determine which paths are ready for review and which require escalation.
chapters.prompt: Before I recommend any retention path, what do our mortgage renewal rules allow, what requires escalation, and who must approve it?

chapters.title: Check what changed outside the bank
chapters.takeaway: Current Canadian mortgage-rate, housing-market, regulatory, and borrower-sentiment signals may change the recommendation or confirm that governed internal evidence is enough.
chapters.prompt: Check current public Canadian mortgage, rate, housing, and regulatory context. What could change the renewal recommendation or confirm internal evidence is enough?

chapters.title: Turn evidence into a reviewable renewal brief
chapters.takeaway: Mortgage Renewal IQ organizes evidence, options, approval owners, confidence, and boundaries so leaders review a scoped recommendation instead of accepting a black-box decision.
chapters.prompt: Based on the evidence, prepare a renewal review brief: prioritized segments, derived risk signals, offer paths, approval owners, privacy boundaries, and decisions that must remain with authorized humans.

chapters.title: Mortgage Renewal IQ recommends; people decide
chapters.takeaway: The agent may recommend prioritization and retention paths for review, but it must not approve, deny, bind, price, or communicate a mortgage renewal offer; determine affordability, creditworthiness, eligibility, or suitability; treat risk scores as customer intent; or bypass authorized human approval.

chat.title: Mortgage Renewal IQ
chat.subtitle: Ask about renewal workload, derived attrition signals, offer guardrails, branch capacity, and approval ownership
chat.emptyTitle: What renewal pressure needs a human decision?
chat.emptyDescription: Connect governed renewal evidence with policies, team context, and current public signals while preserving the privacy and approval boundary.
starterPrompts: Show me the strongest aggregate evidence behind today’s renewal recommendation.
Which recommended offer paths require approval before anyone acts?
What public Canadian context could change our renewal review this week?
Where should the brief be explicit that a human decision is required?
